title: One-Pot Creamy Tomato Chickpeas
description: Chickpeas simmer in a creamy tomato sauce for a fast pantry dinner that is good over toast, rice, or pasta.
substitutions: Use white beans instead of chickpeas.
Use unsweetened oat milk for a dairy-free version and skip the Parmesan.

steps.text: Warm the chickpeas and tomatoes with seasonings.
Stir in milk and simmer until creamy.

cookSteps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet. Add 2 drained cans chickpeas, 1 can diced tomatoes, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon Italian seasoning, and 1/4 teaspoon salt.
Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes soften and the chickpeas are hot.
Stir in 1/2 cup milk or half-and-half and simmer 5 minutes more. Stir in 1/4 cup Parmesan if using and serve over toast, rice, or pasta.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat gently and add a splash of milk if the sauce thickens.

title: Ham, Pea & Potato Hash
description: Cooked potatoes and leftover ham crisp in one skillet with peas for an easy use-it-up meal.
substitutions: Use leftover sausage instead of ham.
Use frozen corn or mixed vegetables instead of peas.

steps.text: Stir in peas and heat through.

cookSteps.text: Melt 1 tablespoon butter or oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 3 cups cooked diced potatoes and cook 8 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned.
Add 1 1/2 cups diced cooked ham, 1/2 teaspoon onion powder, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Cook 4 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add 1 cup frozen peas and cook about 3 minutes, until the peas are hot. Taste before adding any salt because ham is naturally salty.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in a skillet for the crispest potatoes.

title: Cabbage & Cheddar Egg Scramble
description: Thin cabbage cooks down quickly before eggs and cheddar turn it into a simple filling breakfast or light supper.
substitutions: Use mozzarella or Swiss instead of cheddar.
Add a spoonful of diced ham if you have some to use up.

cookSteps.text: Heat 1 teaspoon butter or oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 2 cups thinly sliced cabbage and cook 5 minutes until softened.
Beat 4 eggs with 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/8 teaspoon black pepper. Pour over the cabbage and gently scramble for 3–4 minutes until nearly set.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup shredded cheddar over the eggs, fold gently, and cook 1 minute more until melted.

storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days and reheat gently.

title: Small-Batch Caramel Apple Bread Pudding Cups
description: Four warm bread-pudding cups turn a few slices of bread and one apple into a cozy little dessert with an easy brown-sugar drizzle.
substitutions: Use a pear instead of the apple.
Use brioche, sandwich bread, or leftover rolls.

steps.text: Soak the bread and apple in custard.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease 4 muffin cups or small ramekins. Whisk 1 egg, 3/4 cup milk, 2 tablespoons of the brown sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon. Fold in 3 cups cubed bread and 1 diced apple; let stand 5 minutes.
Divide among the 4 cups and bake about 25 minutes, until puffed and set in the centers.

While they bake, melt 1 tablespoon butter with the remaining 2 tablespoons brown sugar and 2 tablespoons heavy cream or milk in a small saucepan. Simmer 1–2 minutes, stirring, then spoon the warm drizzle over the baked cups.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat briefly before serving; keep extra sauce refrigerated separately.
